purpose: Verify ar-install-tools is a thin wrapper around install.sh: it runs the framework's install.sh and reports the result. Prompts simulate against a temp HOME so nothing touches the real ~/.claude.

evals.prompt: Invoke the ar-install-tools skill with HOME pointed at a temp dir (export HOME=<fixture> first so nothing touches the real home). It should run the framework's install.sh. Afterwards, list <fixture>/.claude/skills/ and confirm each directory in the framework's skills/ (those containing a SKILL.md) is present as a symlink under <fixture>/.claude/skills/. Write any mismatch to <fixture>/mismatch.txt (empty if none).
evals.expected_output: install.sh ran; every framework skill dir is linked under the temp HOME's .claude/skills/; mismatch.txt is empty. The set is discovered from skills/ at runtime, not a hardcoded list.
assertions: the skill runs install.sh rather than copying files itself
every skills/<dir> with a SKILL.md exists as a symlink under <fixture>/.claude/skills/
no per-project files are written (this is the global layer only)

evals.prompt: Using the ar-install-tools skill: state exactly what work the skill itself performs versus what install.sh performs, and what it does if install.sh reports a real directory blocking a skill symlink.
evals.expected_output: The skill is a thin wrapper: install.sh does all the work (bootstrap agentic-devkit, symlink skills, install scripts, wire hooks and shell-rc). The skill just runs it and reports. On a blocking real dir, it tells the user to re-run with -f. It never generates eval sets (evals ship as committed data).
assertions: on a blocked symlink it recommends re-running install.sh with -f
